  <h2>Break-even</h2>
  <p>Cozystack becomes cheaper than Harvester (SUSE) when Harvester (SUSE) support $/node/yr exceeds $1,579 (current: $2,100) — it already does at the current value. One-time migration costs pay back in month 41.</p>
  <h2>Key facts</h2>
  <ul>
    <li>Harvester (SUSE) software is free; commercial support is ~$2100/node/yr (effective $1,800–2,400/node/yr all-in (analyst, research/03 §5) — midpoint; as of 2026-07).</li>
    <li>Contract term default: 12 months (annual subscription (SUSE)).</li>
  </ul>
  <h2>When to choose Harvester (SUSE)</h2>
  <ul>
    <li>Scale below the crossover: at 50 VMs / 1000 VMs Harvester (SUSE) is cheaper at default assumptions — the table above shows it openly.</li>
    <li>Hard vendor-ecosystem dependencies (ISV certifications, existing tooling and runbooks) that outweigh the cost delta.</li>
  </ul>
  <h2>How this is calculated</h2>
  <p>Three cost articles — software (licenses + vendor support), one-time migration and personnel. Hardware and facilities are identical on both sides and excluded; an internal sizing chain (CPU oversubscription 3:1, RAM target 85%, per-platform storage replication, N+1 HA headroom) only produces the node/core/socket counters that licenses bill against. Renewal uplifts apply only after a real renewal event inside the horizon. Default pricing basis is realized (typical negotiated) — conservative against our own headline. Every default carries a source, date and source nature; owner estimates (migration $/VM, personnel days) are labeled as Ænix field data. <a href="/tco-calculator/methodology/">Full methodology, formulas and the complete source list</a>.</p>
  <h2>Frequently asked questions</h2>
  <h3>How much does Harvester (SUSE) cost for 200 VMs over 5 years?</h3>
  <p>At default assumptions (EU region, typical negotiated prices, Q3 2026) the model puts Harvester (SUSE) at $395,581 over 5 years across the three cost articles: software (licenses + vendor support), migration (one-time, target platform only) and personnel (a days-per-month staffing model).</p>
  <h3>Is Cozystack cheaper than Harvester (SUSE)?</h3>
  <p>At 50 VMs: Harvester (SUSE) is $11,038 cheaper. At 200 VMs: Cozystack is $28,666 cheaper (7%). At 1000 VMs: Harvester (SUSE) is $131,101 cheaper. Cozystack becomes cheaper than Harvester (SUSE) when Harvester (SUSE) support $/node/yr exceeds $1,579 (current: $2,100) — it already does at the current value.</p>
  <h3>What does migration from Harvester (SUSE) to Cozystack cost?</h3>
  <p>For 200 VMs the model estimates $60,000 one-time: VMs × $300/VM (owner estimate — Ænix field data: 50 VMs ≈ $15K, typical Cozystack migrations $10–20K total). Professional services or training can be added via the &quot;migration extras&quot; input (default $0). One-time migration costs pay back in month 41.</p>
